prompt: In a proof, a student first shows $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$ by SAS, then writes "therefore $\overline{AC} \cong \overline{DF}$." What is the standard abbreviation for the reason on that second step?
alternativeAnswers: corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent
hint: The reason is a five-letter abbreviation that starts with C.

hints.text: The reason is a five-letter abbreviation that starts with C.
It stands for "Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent."

explanation: CPCTC stands for "Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent."
It is the payoff step: once whole triangles are proven congruent, EVERY matching pair of sides and angles is congruent too.
Order matters — the congruence $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$ pairs $A$ with $D$ and $C$ with $F$, which is what makes $\overline{AC} \cong \overline{DF}$ the right conclusion.

alternativeExplanations.title: Congruence first, parts second
steps: You may only use CPCTC AFTER you have proven the triangles congruent — never as your reason for proving them congruent.
The order in a proof is always: three parts ⇒ congruent triangles (SSS/SAS/ASA/AAS/HL) ⇒ any other part you want (CPCTC).
